description:
## Create ECS task definition and service
**Resource:** ECS task definition and service
**Purpose:** Define the container configuration and service parameters for running fip-mcp on Fargate
**Configuration:**
- Task definition family: fip-mcp
- Launch type: Fargate
- vCPU: 0.25 (256 CPU units)
- Memory: 512 MB
- Network mode: awsvpc
- Container image: 742932328420.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/fip-mcp:latest
- Container port: 3000
- Environment variables from Secrets Manager:
  - ENTRA_TENANT_ID
  - ENTRA_CLIENT_ID
  - DB_CONNECTION_STRING
- Static environment variables:
  - BEDROCK_REGION=us-east-1
  - PORT=3000
  - NODE_ENV=production
  - LOG_LEVEL=info
- Service name: fip-mcp
- Cluster: fortress-tools-cluster
- Desired count: 1
**Verification:** Service runs successfully and passes health checks on port 3000
acceptanceCriteria: ECS task definition is created with correct resource allocation
All environment variables are properly configured from Secrets Manager

## Configure ALB target group and routing
**Resource:** ALB target group and routing rules
**Purpose:** Route incoming HTTP traffic from CloudFlare to the fip-mcp ECS service
**Configuration:**
- Target group name: fip-mcp-tg
- Target type: IP (for Fargate)
- Port: 3000
- Protocol: HTTP
- Health check path: /health
- Health check interval: 30 seconds
- Healthy threshold: 2
- Unhealthy threshold: 3
- Routing rule: Host = api.fortressam.ai AND Path starts with /mcp
- Forward action: fip-mcp target group
**Verification:** Traffic to api.fortressam.ai/mcp/* routes correctly to the service and health checks pass

description:
## Developer Brief — HTTP/SSE MCP Server Foundation
**Spec Reference:** Section 2
### Context
This establishes the core MCP server infrastructure using the @modelcontextprotocol/sdk with SSE transport, providing the foundation for all KB tool operations.
### Scope
- Express.js HTTP server with MCP JSON-RPC 2.0 endpoint
- SSE transport implementation for real-time notifications
- Health check endpoint (no auth required)
- Basic request/response logging
- NOT included: tool implementations (separate stories)
### Technical Notes
- Use @modelcontextprotocol/sdk SSEServerTransport class
- Server listens on port from PORT env var (default 3000)
- Follow FIP logging standards with structured JSON output
- Standard Express middleware stack (helmet, compression, etc.)
### Dependencies
- @modelcontextprotocol/sdk npm package
- Express.js HTTP framework selection
### Open Questions
None
acceptanceCriteria: Server accepts POST /mcp requests with valid JSON-RPC 2.0 format
GET /mcp/sse establishes SSE connection successfully
GET /health returns 200 OK without authentication
Server starts on configured PORT and logs startup message
Invalid JSON-RPC requests return proper error responses
SSE connections handle client disconnections gracefully

title: As a security engineer, I want to implement Entra OAuth token validation so that only authenticated FIP users can access KB operations
description:
## Developer Brief — Entra OAuth Token Validation
**Spec Reference:** Section 4
### Context
Implements comprehensive JWT validation against Entra's JWKS endpoint to ensure all KB operations are authenticated and authorized using the same token pattern as other FIP services.
### Scope
- Bearer token extraction from Authorization header
- JWT signature validation against Entra JWKS
- Claims validation (aud, tid, exp) per FIP standards
- Token user info extraction (oid, groups, roles)
- Proper 401/403 error responses
### Technical Notes
- Use jsonwebtoken + jwks-rsa or @azure/msal-node for validation
- Cache JWKS responses with appropriate TTL
- Extract user_id (oid), groups, and roles claims for downstream use
- Follow FIP auth error response format
### Dependencies
- ENTRA_TENANT_ID and ENTRA_CLIENT_ID from Secrets Manager
- JWT validation library selection
### Open Questions
None
acceptanceCriteria: Requests without Authorization header return 401 Unauthorized
Invalid or expired JWT tokens return 401 Unauthorized
Valid tokens with wrong tenant or audience return 401 Unauthorized
Valid tokens extract user_id, groups, and roles for use by tools
JWKS responses are cached to minimize external calls
Auth failures are logged with appropriate detail level

description:
## Developer Brief — CORS Configuration for FIP Domains
**Spec Reference:** Section 2
### Context
Configures CORS to allow cross-origin requests from known FIP applications (FAIT, FIRM, NEXUS) running on different domains while supporting authentication headers.
### Scope
- Allow specific FIP origins: *.fortressam.ai subdomains
- Support preflight OPTIONS requests
- Allow Authorization header and other necessary headers
- Enable credentials for authenticated requests
- NOT a wildcard CORS policy - security-conscious domain list
### Technical Notes
- Use cors Express middleware with dynamic origin function
- Allow origins: https://*.fortressam.ai (dev and prod subdomains)
- Allow methods: GET, POST, OPTIONS
- Allow headers: Authorization, Content-Type, Accept
- credentials: true (required for auth bearer tokens)
### Dependencies
- Express cors middleware
### Open Questions
None
acceptanceCriteria: CORS headers allow requests from https://fait.fortressam.ai
CORS headers allow requests from https://fait.dev.fortressam.ai
CORS headers allow requests from https://firm.dev.fortressam.ai
CORS headers allow requests from https://nexus.fortressam.ai
Preflight OPTIONS requests return appropriate CORS headers
Authorization header is allowed in cross-origin requests
Credentials are supported for authenticated requests

parentTitle: Implement search_kb tool with auto-scoping security enforcement
title: As an AI agent, I want to search Knowledge Bases with automatic security scoping so that I can retrieve relevant content while respecting access controls
description:
## Developer Brief — search_kb Tool Implementation
**Spec Reference:** Section 3.1
### Context
The primary KB search tool that all FIP applications will use instead of direct bedrock-agent-runtime calls, with automatic security filtering based on KB type and user identity.
### Scope
- MCP tool registration and parameter validation
- Bedrock Agent Runtime Retrieve API integration
- Auto-scoping security filter injection per KB type
- Entitlement validation before KB access
- Error handling for invalid KB IDs and access denials
- NOT included: entitlement management (separate story)
### Technical Notes
- Use @aws-sdk/client-bedrock-agent-runtime
- Follow KB inventory mapping from spec section 2
- Merge auto-injected security filters with caller-provided filters using AND logic
- Return structured response matching MCP tool pattern
### Dependencies
- Bedrock IAM permissions from infrastructure setup
- KB entitlement system (can use fallback config initially)
### Open Questions
None
acceptanceCriteria: Tool validates required parameters (query, kb_id) and rejects invalid requests
Personal KB automatically injects user_id filter from token.oid
Team KB requires team_id in filters and validates team membership
Project KB requires project_id and validates project access
Corp and NEXUS KBs apply no automatic filtering (org-wide access)
Results include content, metadata, and relevance_score fields
Invalid kb_id returns 400 UNKNOWN_KB error
Unauthorized access returns 403 NOT_ENTITLED error

parentTitle: Implement list_kbs tool and entitlement system
title: As a FIP application, I want to discover available Knowledge Bases for the current user so that I can present appropriate KB options in the UI
description:
## Developer Brief — list_kbs Tool Implementation
**Spec Reference:** Section 3.2
### Context
Provides KB discovery functionality so FIP applications can dynamically present users with only the KBs they have permission to access, supporting both database and configuration-based entitlements.
### Scope
- MCP tool that returns accessible KBs with metadata
- Database query against kb_entitlements table (when available)
- Fallback to static JSON configuration file
- Group-based entitlement resolution from token.groups
- Read/write permission indication per KB
- NOT included: entitlement management UI (admin functionality)
### Technical Notes
- Query FAIT v2 DB kb_entitlements table first if available
- Fall back to FALLBACK_ENTITLEMENTS_CONFIG JSON file
- Always include NEXUS KB (WHB6WU9CVW) for authenticated users
- Return kb_type field mapped from KB inventory
### Dependencies
- DB_CONNECTION_STRING configuration (optional)
- FALLBACK_ENTITLEMENTS_CONFIG file path
- KB inventory mapping from spec
### Open Questions
FAIT v2 DB may not exist initially - fallback config bridges this gap
acceptanceCriteria: Tool returns array of accessible KBs with id, type, description, writable fields
Database entitlements take priority over fallback config when DB available
Fallback config supports both user-specific and group-based entitlements
NEXUS KB (WHB6WU9CVW) always included as read-only for authenticated users
Group memberships from token.groups properly resolve to KB entitlements
Default entitlements apply to all users when specified in config

title: As an AI agent, I want to add content to Knowledge Bases asynchronously so that I can ingest documents without blocking on completion
description:
## Developer Brief — add_to_kb Tool Implementation
**Spec Reference:** Section 3.3
### Context
Enables content ingestion into FORGE KBs with proper async handling, write entitlement enforcement, and metadata validation for audit trails.
### Scope
- MCP tool accepting content and metadata for KB ingestion
- Write entitlement validation before proceeding
- Bedrock StartIngestionJob API integration
- Immediate job_id return for async polling
- Metadata validation (source, created_by required)
- NOT included: job status polling (separate get_job_status tool)
### Technical Notes
- Use @aws-sdk/client-bedrock-agent-runtime StartIngestionJob
- Validate metadata.source and metadata.created_by presence
- For Project KBs: require metadata.project_id
- For Corp/NEXUS KBs: require forge-kb-admin role
- Return structured response with job_id and status='queued'
### Dependencies
- Bedrock IAM permissions for StartIngestionJob
- Write entitlement system from list_kbs implementation
### Open Questions
S3 trigger vs direct ingestion approach - Tony to verify KB data source config
acceptanceCriteria: Tool validates required parameters (kb_id, content, metadata)
Write entitlement check prevents unauthorized ingestion attempts
Metadata validation enforces source and created_by fields
Project KB ingestion requires metadata.project_id field
Corp and NEXUS KB writes require forge-kb-admin role
Returns job_id immediately without waiting for completion
Error responses include appropriate codes (WRITE_NOT_ENTITLED, METADATA_REQUIRED)

## Developer Brief — get_kb_metadata Tool Implementation
**Spec Reference:** Section 3.4
### Context
Provides KB inspection capabilities for administrators and applications to monitor Knowledge Base status, document counts, and last update information.
### Scope
- MCP tool returning KB statistics and configuration
- Bedrock GetKnowledgeBase and ListIngestionJobs API integration
- Read entitlement validation before allowing metadata access
- Document count derivation and last updated calculation
- NOT included: detailed document listing or content inspection
### Technical Notes
- Use GetKnowledgeBase for basic KB info and data_source_id
- Use ListIngestionJobs to calculate document_count and last_updated
- Derive last_updated from most recent completed ingestion job
- Map kb_type from KB inventory configuration
### Dependencies
- Bedrock IAM permissions for metadata APIs
- Read entitlement system from list_kbs
### Open Questions
None

description:
## Developer Brief — get_job_status Universal Polling Tool
**Spec Reference:** Section 3.5
### Context
Implements the standard FIP MCP async polling contract that all async tools use, starting with KB ingestion jobs and extensible to future async operations.
### Scope
- MCP tool accepting job_id and returning standardized status
- GetIngestionJob API integration for KB job polling
- Extensible job routing for future job types
- Standard async response format (queued/running/complete/failed)
- In-memory job tracking for MVP (DB-backed in future)
### Technical Notes
- Use GetIngestionJob for KB ingestion job IDs
- Return status, result, error, percent_complete fields per FIP contract
- For MVP: in-memory job type routing is acceptable
- Future: add jobs table for cross-restart persistence
- This establishes the pattern all FIP MCP async tools must follow
### Dependencies
- Bedrock IAM permissions for GetIngestionJob
- Job ID format from add_to_kb implementation
### Open Questions
None
acceptanceCriteria: Tool accepts job_id parameter and validates format
Routes KB ingestion job_ids to GetIngestionJob API calls
Returns standardized status (queued/running/complete/failed)
Includes result object when status=complete
Includes error string when status=failed
Percent_complete field populated when available from Bedrock

7. **S3 trigger vs direct ingestion** - add_to_kb implementation approach depends on KB data source configuration. Need Tony to verify actual setup.

8. **ECR repository creation** - Timeline for creating fip-mcp ECR repository before first build.

title: Configure CloudFlare routing for /mcp paths with SSE support
description:
Set up CloudFlare configuration to route api.fortressam.ai/mcp/* traffic to the fip-mcp service with proper SSE timeout handling and CORS passthrough.

**CloudFlare configuration requirements:**
- Route: https://api.fortressam.ai/mcp/* → ALB (same ALB as other FIP services)
- SSE timeout: Set proxy timeout to 300s+ for /mcp/sse path to prevent early connection termination
- Response buffering: Disable for /mcp/sse to allow real-time event streaming
- CORS passthrough: Do not modify Access-Control-Allow-* headers set by the service
- Cache policy: Cache-bypass (no-store) for /mcp/* paths

**Coordination with Rob Nethery required for:**
- Domain path confirmation (api.fortressam.ai vs separate subdomain)
- SSE-specific timeout and buffering configuration
- CORS header passthrough setup
acceptanceCriteria: CloudFlare routes /mcp/* traffic to correct ALB target
SSE connections on /mcp/sse maintain 300+ second timeouts
Response buffering is disabled for SSE endpoint
Service-set CORS headers pass through unmodified
No caching applied to /mcp/* API endpoints
End-to-end connectivity verified from external clients

title: Migrate FIRM from direct bedrock-agent-runtime to add_to_kb MCP tool
description:
## FIRM Migration to fip-mcp
**Before:** FIRM's firm-transcriber Batch container calls bedrock-agent-runtime:StartIngestionJob directly to push meeting summaries to Personal KB
**After:** FIRM calls fip-mcp add_to_kb tool via HTTP/MCP for all KB ingestion operations
**Migration Steps:**
1. Replace bedrock-agent-runtime SDK calls with HTTP client to fip-mcp
2. Update authentication to use Entra bearer token instead of AWS credentials
3. Modify ingestion call to use add_to_kb tool format with proper metadata
4. Update error handling to process MCP error responses
5. Add job status polling using get_job_status tool
**Validation:** FIRM meeting summary ingestion works through fip-mcp with same functional outcome
**Rollback:** Revert to direct bedrock-agent-runtime calls if fip-mcp integration fails
acceptanceCriteria: FIRM no longer makes direct bedrock-agent-runtime calls
Meeting summaries are successfully ingested via fip-mcp add_to_kb tool
Authentication uses Entra tokens instead of AWS credentials
Job status polling is implemented for ingestion monitoring
Error handling properly processes MCP error responses
Performance and reliability match previous direct integration
